subject: mathematics
question_text: Find the value of tan20° + tan40° + √3 tan20° tan40°.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.85, chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 15. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split gives one mark to starting from tan(20° + 40°) and one to rearranging the expansion into the expression that was asked for. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A prints ten very short answers of 2 marks each and the student writes all ten; Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations supplies two of those slots on almost every paper. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name the formula you use and how you finish.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Start from tan(20° + 40°)
steps.margin_note: First mark. 20° + 40° = 60° and tan60° = √3, which is the √3 already standing in the question.
steps.memory_tip: 20° + 40° = 60°, and tan60° = √3 — the same √3 the question shows.

recall.must_convey: That the two angles add to 60°, so the tan(A+B) formula is written with tan60° = √3 on the right.
accept: twenty plus forty is sixty so start from tan sixty which is root three
use the tan A plus B formula with the two angles
write tan of twenty plus forty equals root three and expand
twenty plus forty ante sixty, tan sixty root three

steps.why: The √3 in the third term is a hint. It is tan60°, and 60° is the sum of the two angles in the question, so the sum formula is the right starting point.
common_mistakes: Trying to find tan20° and tan40° separately.

steps.label: Rearrange to the asked expression
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Cross multiply, expand the bracket, then move the product term to the left side.
steps.memory_tip: Cross multiply, then move √3 tan20° tan40° to the left. What is left on the right is √3.
lines: Adding √3 tan20° tan40° to both sides:

recall.must_convey: That cross multiplying and moving the product term across gives the value √3.
accept: cross multiply and expand root three into the bracket
move the product term to the left and the answer is root three
cross multiply chesi term move cheste root three vasthundi
root three minus root three tan twenty tan forty, so it cancels

steps.why: The √3 tan20° tan40° that the question adds is exactly the term the expansion subtracts, so the two cancel and only √3 is left.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply √3 into both terms of the bracket.
Leaving the answer as √3(1 − tan20° tan40°).
